Felix listing what Trust Wallet still isn't good enough at is rarer than any feature launch.

He says it's solid for crypto "except meme trading," and puts five fixes on a 2-3 week clock: one price source instead of several, 5x faster refresh, lower fees, intent-based search, readable order history.

He called them basic. That's the right word. This is plumbing, and plumbing is what decides whether meme traders on BNB Chain stay in the wallet or drift back to a Telegram bot with unlimited approvals.

Three weeks is a short clock. But after watching what shipped in the last twelve months, I'd take that bet. "A 9 year old wallet getting younger" is a good line, and so far it's also true.

Thanks all for reaching out about this, really appreciate you all and the support but a few thoughts on the current market that have led me to this decision:

1) I am doing everything alone, from building to customer support to working other jobs that take my time and energy as I am bootstrapped. It's a lot, but the ability to scale for independent operators like me just is not there as you often have to wait for customer payments via Stripe to clear via settlement on the banking side. This can take anywhere from 2-3 business days depending. What does this mean? The more customers you have, the more cash you must be able to float (I cannot afford, say, 20k in API fees to float larger customers, I just can't)

2) On the topic of API fees and what this means: you are throwing your money away to companies like Seedance as a developer. They fail you for every single generation your customers ask for, regardless of how innocent, as sensitive content. I currently use Seedance 2 via Replicate. Literally nothing will pass muster. Why should I be at their mercy to make my product look bad? New customers to the AI scene don't understand overly egregious content moderation and instead blame YOUR product because they have no clue how some of this works, they're merely end users. This is incredibly frustrating for a number of reasons. Which brings me to 3...

3) No one is training their own solution as much in house. Everyone in the space is becoming wrappers around other models. Every time I throw money away on failed generations via Seedance that result ultimately in requests for refunds is a missed opportunity for me to train and refine the current open source models that I can own and operate for far cheaper in-house. Not to mention, I am working on more immersive media that you will all see eventually. This means that focusing on NoSpoon's current direction, as-is, reliant on other providers without in-house models and solutions simply makes no sense. So, I am going to be reallocating my efforts to training, improvements, more immersive media, and video intelligence (which the agent has, it's just not public yet). All of which to say: my bet on the future is an interactive one. Not the current biz model of wrapping around model providers and crossing your fingers that nothing got content moderated that day. So that also brings me to...

4) There is a massive distribution problem in the space. Content that is made with AI, where does it go? Who monetizes it? Who is engaging with it? What is the end result? This is my current stealth venture and massive focus in conjunction with adtech. I do not see a great path forwards if there is no end-to-end distribution of either content on its own or else interactive ways to create and co-collaborate in realtime with AI.

5) People can barely afford groceries. Gas is rising. The general population is being told AI is going to kill everyone with a 10% chance or sth by the end of the decade. How does it make sense to spin your wheels in this environment throwing money away to other model providers when the consumers have no end path towards monetization, and even if by some stroke of miracle they are engaged and excited by AI + new to the space after hearing all of this doomer rhetoric, they then hit your product and it has a model like Seedance that instantly fails them for content moderation on the most innocent prompts there are? How do you think that is going to land for new consumers? Badly, especially given the cost of these models and your end product. So, it leaves a bad taste in everyone's mouth but the model provider that you're wrapping around and paying on occasion. It is not sustainable.

6) People want to have fun. They want to enjoy creating (or sometimes just viewing!) without breaking the bank. They want to be elevated in their endeavors and not drained dry for metrics at the end of each quarter. Pricing at present has steadily climbed, but with the advent of h3 (so thankful for them) there's a new opportunity to at least target a smaller price point with post-training and newer methods that can achieve lower costs and higher quality. But, until distribution is solved, nothing is really going to move the needle here. Everyone is trying to figure this out.

Anyway, all of this to say: until I figure out a few of these pain points and really take the time to actually get a few ideas together, it doesn't make sense to brand a product so dependent on others at this stage. So, I'm taking the time to corner more distribution, adtech solutions, and ultimately model independence to some degree in order to create more affordability for newcomers in an increasingly hostile economic environment for all.

James Talarico said, "The American flag is such a complicated symbol for most of us."

That was not the case on September 11, 2001.

Later that very day, 116,000 US flags were bought at Wal-Mart locations all across the nation (vs. 6,400 on 9/11/2020).

From that Tuesday through Thursday, Wal-Mart sold around 450,000 American flags.

Kmart sold about 200,000 US flags the first few days after 9/11. 

Add in Home Depot, Kroger, Target, and hundreds and hundreds of small stores all over this wounded country.

One major flag dealer said they sold a year and a half of inventory in the first week after 9/11.

Colonial Flag said it shipped more than a million flags to retailers in the first 10 days after 9/11, with demand up 2,000%. 

Within days, you saw more houses displaying flags than those that didn't.

And when you saw a house without a flag, you immediately had a visceral response. 

Heartbroken Americans became BOLD PATRIOTS in an instant.

We stood together. 

Our flag wasn't a complicated symbol at all. 

It was the symbol of American pride, hope, strength, and unity. 

Think about in November when you head to the polls.
